additional_official_sources_fetched.title: 42 CFR 435.552 — Demonstrating community engagement
additional_official_sources_fetched.confirmed: Codified regulatory text. (a)(1)-(7) list the seven ways to demonstrate community engagement for a month. (a)(6) monthly income not less than the FLSA section 6 minimum wage multiplied by 80 hours. (a)(7) six-month average AND is a seasonal worker as described in 26 U.S.C. 45R(d)(5)(B). (b) defines community service, educational program, work (including unpaid work other than community service) and work program. (c) enrolment status is determined by the school. (d) less-than-half-time hours = credit hours x 3 x 4.33. (e)(1) States may not combine education hours with another activity if enrolled at least half-time. (f)(2) 'The agency must determine the monthly income based on the individual's MAGI-based income, for their MAGI-based household, as defined at 435.603'. (g)(1) seasonal-worker averaging path; (g)(2) same MAGI-based household measure

additional_official_sources_fetched.title: 42 CFR 435.551 — Applicable individual
additional_official_sources_fetched.confirmed: An applicable individual is not a specified excluded individual under 435.554 and is eligible/enrolled under 435.119 (adult group) or in a qualifying 1115(a)(2) demonstration, and is at least 19 and under 65, not pregnant, and not entitled to or enrolled in Medicare Part A or enrolled in Part B

additional_official_sources_fetched.title: 42 CFR 435.554 — Specified excluded individuals

additional_official_sources_fetched.title: AB 2161 (2025-2026), Chapter 209 - Medi-Cal eligibility: work or community engagement (Welf. & Inst. Code 14005.69)

(d)(1) an applicant must demonstrate it 'for one month immediately preceding the month during which the individual applies'. findings.topic: Seven ways to satisfy the requirement for a month
findings.value: 80 hours of work; 80 hours of community service; 80 hours in a work program; enrolment in an educational programme at least half-time; a combination of those activities totalling 80 hours; monthly income of at least the federal minimum wage x 80 ($580 in 2026); or, for a seasonal worker only, a six-month average monthly income of at least $580

findings.topic: What income the $580 test actually measures
findings.value: MAGI-based income for the MAGI-based household, as defined at 42 CFR 435.603 — not 'gross income'
findings.note: 42 CFR 435.552(f)(2) and (g)(2) both require the MAGI-based household measure. DHCS ACWDL 25-30 (preliminary, December 30 2025) says 'total gross income'; the codified federal rule (effective July 31 2026) says MAGI-based household income. For a property owner these differ, because MAGI uses NET rental income

findings.topic: Does unearned income count toward the $580
findings.value: Yes. Capital gains, interest (including tax-exempt interest), dividends and NET rental and royalty income are all included in MAGI, and MAGI is the measure the rule requires
findings.note: This is the load-bearing answer for a person with $0 earned income: no wages are required. It also means a trading LOSS or rental expenses reduce the figure, and gross rents overstate it

findings.topic: Is the six-month averaging path available to a trader with irregular gains
findings.value: No, not on the federal rule. 42 CFR 435.552(a)(7) and (g)(1) require that the individual IS a seasonal worker as described in 26 U.S.C. 45R(d)(5)(B)
findings.note: The CMS fact sheet agrees in substance: '$580 per month in 2026; for seasonal workers, there is a different calculation.' DHCS's member-facing letter is broader ('people whose hours change frequently or who have seasonal jobs'). The federal regulation is the operative text and is narrower; the divergence is flagged, not resolved. Own-account trading is not seasonal labour

findings.topic: Lump-sum treatment
findings.value: 'An amount received as a lump sum is counted as income only in the month received'
findings.note: Directly relevant to irregular trading settlements: a large settlement counts in the month received, which can satisfy that month's $580 test on its own

findings.topic: Who is subject at all
findings.value: An 'applicable individual' — not a specified excluded individual, and eligible/enrolled in the adult group (42 CFR 435.119) or a qualifying 1115 demonstration, aged at least 19 and under 65, not pregnant, not entitled to or enrolled in Medicare Part A or enrolled in Part B

findings.topic: How long a window a State may test at application
findings.value: At least one, but not more than 3 consecutive months, as specified in the State plan, immediately preceding the month of application
findings.note: This resolves the earlier '1 month vs 3 months' ambiguity on the site: it is a State-plan choice inside a federal 1-to-3-month band. California's preliminary ACWDL 25-30 uses the single month immediately preceding application, which is inside the band

findings.topic: Renewal window for an existing member
findings.value: 1 or more months between the most recent determination or redetermination and the date the renewal is due, whether or not consecutive
findings.note: Matches DHCS MEDIL I26-25: 'in any month since your last renewal'

findings.topic: Does unpaid work count
findings.value: Yes. 'Work' means work in exchange for money, work in exchange for goods or services (in-kind work), and unpaid work other than community service
findings.note: Relevant to a property manager: unpaid work is expressly inside the definition of work. Whether managing one's OWN property is 'work' for this purpose is not settled by any official source reviewed and is left unverified

findings.topic: What counts as community service
findings.value: Unpaid work, voluntary or court-ordered, with a structured programme, for the direct benefit of the community, under the auspices of public or non-profit organisations, which must provide oversight, must not serve a partisan purpose, and must track the activity type, dates, hours and a point of contact who can confirm the hours

findings.topic: Education route
findings.value: At least half-time enrolment is its own route; enrolment status is determined by the school. Less-than-half-time enrolment converts to hours as credit hours x 3 x 4.33 weeks

findings.topic: Combining activities
findings.value: Activities may be combined to reach 80 hours, but States are NOT permitted to combine educational programme hours with another activity if the individual is already enrolled at least half-time
findings.note: 42 CFR 435.552(a)(5) and (e)(1). A detail the site's earlier 'any mix of the above' row did not carry

findings.topic: 2026 income figures for a single person
findings.value: 100% FPL annual $15,960; 138% FPL annual $22,025; 138% FPL monthly $1,836; 400% FPL monthly $5,320
findings.note: Cross-checked against the DHCS 2026 FPL Calculation Chart (monthly values, rounded up to the next higher dollar) and the DHCS Eligibility by Federal Poverty Level table. All three official sources agree

findings.topic: Why the 2026 guidelines look unusual
findings.value: Because of the October 2025 federal government shutdown, BLS did not publish CPI-U for that month, so the 2026 guidelines compare the average CPI-U for the 11 available months of 2025 (excluding October) with the average for all 12 months of 2024
findings.note: New detail not previously published on the site. It matters because the 2026 FPL figures drive every threshold above

findings.topic: The multi-state lawsuit
findings.value: Commonwealth of Massachusetts et al. v. Mehmet Oz, filed June 29 2026, co-led by California, Massachusetts and New Jersey; 24 attorneys general plus the governors of Kentucky and Pennsylvania
findings.note: California is a co-lead, not the lead plaintiff. The complaint targets the IFC's narrowing of the 'medically frail' protection and other APA and coercion claims

findings.topic: California budget impact
findings.value: Approximately $1.3 billion General Fund in 2026-27 for H.R.1 costs; total projected H.R.1 disenrollment 44,000 in 2026-27 and 1.3 million by 2029-30; the work and community engagement requirement alone projects 43,000 and 1.1 million; county administration one-time augmentation $709M including $196.8M General Fund
findings.note: These are DHCS budget PROJECTIONS, not realised counts

findings.topic: How many states are affected
findings.note: Official sources disagree. The CMS fact sheet says '43 states and the District of Columbia provide coverage to these populations'; CRS R48633 (as previously logged on this site) counts 40 expansion states plus DC. Both are official. The number is therefore left BLANK here rather than choosing one

findings.topic: Age of a dependent child for the caregiver exclusion
findings.note: CMS's own fact sheet is internally inconsistent: its prose says 'children under 14 years of age' while its exemption table says 'a dependent child 13 years of age and under'. The codified rule is unambiguous — 42 CFR 435.554 defines 'dependent child' as a child 13 years of age or under, and DHCS ACWDL 25-30 says 'age 13 years of age and under'. Left blank because the CMS document contradicts itself; the codified value is 13 or under

findings.topic: When the rule takes effect in California
findings.note: DHCS publishes both dates. ACWDL 25-30 and the MEDIL I26-25 body say January 1 2027; the enclosed member letter says the rules 'will not go into effect until March 2027'; the DHCS Medi-Cal Changes page separates the work rule (January 1) from the first six-month eligibility checks (March 1). Left blank as a single date; both are published on the site

findings.topic: Federal tax treatment of Kalshi event contracts
findings.note: No IRS guidance on event contracts was located. uscode.house.gov was under maintenance during this session. Left blank and flagged; no treatment is asserted

findings.topic: California has ENACTED its own work-rule statute
findings.value: AB 2161, Chapter 209 (2025-2026), amending Welfare & Institutions Code section 14005.69; approved by the Governor and filed with the Secretary of State on September 14, 2026
findings.note: This is the single most important source for a California reader and it postdates every document the site was originally built on: DHCS ACWDL 25-30 (December 30 2025, expressly preliminary), the federal interim final rule (June 3 2026, effective July 31 2026) and DHCS MEDIL I 26-25 (September 11 2026, an outreach letter). Where ACWDL 25-30 and the enacted statute differ, the enacted statute governs. Earlier sessions did not have this source

findings.topic: What the $580 income test measures, under enacted California law
findings.value: 'A total monthly income, using modified adjusted gross income (MAGI)-based financial methods ... for their individual MAGI-based household budget' of at least the federal minimum wage multiplied by 80 hours
findings.note: Welf. & Inst. Code 14005.69(e)(6). This settles the gross-versus-MAGI question that DHCS ACWDL 25-30 left open, and it matches the federal rule at 42 CFR 435.552(f)(2) exactly. For a property owner MAGI means NET rent after expenses, not gross receipts. Earned income is still not required - MAGI includes capital gains, interest and net rental income

findings.topic: Is six-month averaging available for irregular trading income, under enacted California law
findings.value: No. It requires that the individual 'is a seasonal worker, as described in Section 45R(d)(5)(B) of the federal Internal Revenue Code of 1986'
findings.note: Welf. & Inst. Code 14005.69(e)(7), identical in effect to 42 CFR 435.552(g)(1). Two independent authorities - the enacted state statute and the codified federal regulation - both limit the averaging path to seasonal workers. ACWDL 25-30's 'fluctuating income' row and MEDIL I 26-25's 'people whose hours change frequently' wording are outreach simplifications that the enacted text does not support. Own-account Kalshi trading is not seasonal labour under 26 U.S.C. 45R(d)(5)(B)

findings.topic: How far back California looks at application, and at renewal
findings.value: At application: exactly one month immediately preceding the month of application. At renewal: any one month between the most recent determination or redetermination and the next regularly scheduled redetermination
findings.note: Welf. & Inst. Code 14005.69(d)(1) and (d)(2). This resolves the earlier site ambiguity about whether the federal band of 'at least one, but not more than 3 consecutive months' (42 CFR 435.556(a)(1)) meant California might look back three months. California chose ONE month. For renewal the months need not be consecutive, which matches MEDIL I 26-25's 'in any month since your last renewal'

findings.topic: What happens if the county cannot verify compliance
findings.value: The county must issue a notice of noncompliance and give 30 calendar days from the date the notice is RECEIVED; Medi-Cal services continue during that 30-day period for an enrolled member
findings.note: Welf. & Inst. Code 14005.69(k)(1)(A)-(C)(i). The 30 days run from receipt, not from the date on the notice - a materially better protection than a mailing-date reading, and worth knowing before missing a deadline

findings.topic: What if the county's own data sources disagree
findings.value: Where there is a conflict in reliable data sources that adversely impacts eligibility, the county must ask the applicant or beneficiary to confirm the information BEFORE taking any adverse action on the application or renewal
findings.note: Welf. & Inst. Code 14005.69(i). This is a California-specific protection with no federal equivalent in 42 CFR 435.556. For someone whose income is irregular and whose data-match results may conflict (FTB, EDD, IRS), this is the provision to cite
